messages:
evan (support): FYI escalated ticket from Acme — multiple customers seeing auth failures + retry storms after SDK updates. Opening thread to coordinate.
samir (sdk-engineer): Can you drop a short repro and which SDK versions are affected?
evan (support): Repro (from reported steps):

1) Install python-sdk==0.10.0
2) Make a simple completion call

curl example they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Observed: immediate 401 (invalid auth) for some requests, then client retries -> a bunch of 429s and duplicate billing for some customers. Logs attached by customer show header present but downstream gateway rejects: "missing api key header". They also tested ts-sdk@0.9.4 and go-sdk v0.8.3 with same symptoms.
maya (devex): This smells like the OpenAPI rename we merged last week (api_key -> client_api_key / header renames). If the generator templates weren't updated with a backward-compatible header alias, older clients might still be sending the old header name while the gateway expects the new one. Which exact generator commit was used to produce those SDK packages?
evan (support): From the package manifests customers shared: python 0.10.0 published 2025-11-28 (installer shows generator hash abc123). Older working version python 0.9.7 works for them. TS 0.9.4 is newer and exhibits same issue. They pinned to older releases and problem stopped.
samir (sdk-engineer): I checked main — we merged an OpenAPI change (PR #4218) renaming header model field. There was a follow-up template change for the generator (PR #4229) but CI job that regenerates packaged SDKs failed last Friday due to checksum mismatch and no new releases were cut. So packages published may be from a partially updated pipeline.
alice (platform-ci): CI excerpt:
```
openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g typescript-axios -o out/ts
# exit 0
git diff --exit-code || (echo "generated artifacts differ" && exit 2)
```
Our job returned non-zero because of whitespace ordering diffs from the generator version bump. The regen step was skipped from the release job then accidentally published the older artifact. I'm digging into the checksum mismatch.
maya (devex): Short-term mitigations:
- Gateway: accept both header names (old and new) for now. Minimal change in routing layer.
- SDKs: release a tiny patch that sets both headers when present (or sets new header if old is used).
- Support: tell affected customers to pin to the last known-good SDK (0.9.7 for python) or make a curl change to send the new header: `-H 'X-Client-Api-Key: $TOKEN'`.

Quick TS snippet to set compatibility header (will open patch):
```ts
// in request interceptor
const token = getToken();
config.headers = { ...config.headers, 'X-Client-Api-Key': token, 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` };
```
samir (sdk-engineer): I'll open a compatibility PR for python/ts/go that adds fallback header behavior + tests. Also will trigger a manual regen with pinned openapi-generator version to eliminate whitespace churn. PRs: #4283 (ts), #4284 (py), #4285 (go). ETA for patches + regens: ~4 hours. I'll add changelog entries noting the header alias and recommend pinning guidance.
evan (support): Thanks — please also include a short customer-facing blurb we can paste to the ticket (what happened, temporary workaround, ETA for patch). Also flag any billing exposures where duplicate retries caused charges — we'll coordinate refunds if needed.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: gateway config updated to accept both headers in canary (us-west-2) — canary healthy after 5m :thumbsup:
samir (sdk-engineer): CI follow-up: I'll force the regen using openapi-generator-cli v6.6.0 and add a deterministic prettier step to smooth whitespace diffs. Will then re-run the release pipeline and unpublish the bad microversions if needed.
evan (support): Perfect — I'll message customers with the workaround + ETA. Keep us posted on PR merges so we can close the escalation. :pray:
